assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling made aryl amines, ubiquitous in pharmaceuticals and materials, accessible by a general, predictable bond construction. The ligand-design logic (bulky, electron-rich phosphines and carbenes) turned a hard transformation into routine practice, which is the kind of general method I weigh most.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the catalytic, ligand-controlled versions and the mechanistic understanding. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor and a possible credit complication, but the two-person configuration is fair and clean.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use in medicinal and process chemistry and in industry, with extensive independent confirmation. The 2010 cross-coupling prize covered C-C coupling only, so recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether Kosugi/Migita precedent should share credit, from my recollection of the history rather than verification.
Overlap with the earlier cross-coupling prize may make some members regard it as a continuation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective C-H functionalization changes retrosynthetic logic by treating C-H bonds as functional groups. Directing-group, ligand- and template-controlled methods now appear across total synthesis, late-stage drug diversification and industry, and this is a substantial conceptual and practical advance in efficiency.
assessment.attribution: Yu (ligand-enabled Pd C-H activation, remote and meta selectivity), Hartwig (Ir-catalyzed borylation) and Sanford (Pd/high-valent mechanisms, fluorination) are distinct pillars. The field is broad, so any three-person selection leaves out important contributors such as Daugulis and Smith.
assessment.maturity: Broad independent adoption, though some methods remain substrate-specific and industrial uptake is uneven. Reasonably mature, with the field still maturing.
uncertainties: Hartwig is also credited under B060, so a joint outcome with that candidate is uncertain.
Which sub-theme (borylation, directed Pd, undirected) is the decisive discovery is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry made routine, automated solid-phase oligonucleotide synthesis possible, underpinning PCR primers, sequencing, gene synthesis and oligonucleotide therapeutics. It is plainly molecule-making chemistry with enormous downstream effect.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite method, so a sole laureate is defensible. Hood is credited here for automation and instrumentation, and I recall Beaucage as a co-developer of the key reagent, but he is absent from the supplied credit, which limits the configuration.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, more than 40 years of ubiquitous use. Recognition is late, but not obsolete in relevance, as the oligonucleotide drug field is booming.
uncertainties: Incomplete credit list (possible missing co-inventor) constrains a fair prize.
Hood's role is more automation than chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened radical and single-electron pathways to mild, general bond constructions that are now widely used in drug discovery and total synthesis. It is a genuine change in how chemists build bonds.
assessment.attribution: MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson published the foundational 2008 reports, and Nicewicz, König and others added key work. MacMillan is already a laureate (2021, organocatalysis), which may argue for a different configuration. Fukuzumi and others complicate the earlier history.
assessment.maturity: Roughly 15 years old, with high independent confirmation and industrial uptake. Reasonably timely, possibly slightly early relative to the longest-established methods.
uncertainties: Prior prize for MacMillan and the question of priority among overlapping groups.
Scalability and reproducibility in industry are still debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolable stable carbenes (N-heterocyclic and cyclic alkyl amino carbenes) created a new class of ligands and organocatalysts. They underlie robust Ru metathesis catalysts and modern cross-coupling catalysts, and expanded main-group bonding concepts.
assessment.attribution: Arduengo isolated the first crystalline NHC and Bertrand the earlier stable phosphinocarbene and later CAACs. Nolan, Bode and Rovis are application-oriented contributors, so the two-person core is the natural allocation.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, thoroughly confirmed and used in industry. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Bertrand's 1988 carbene priority versus Arduengo's 1991 NHC is a nuanced credit question.
Some of the impact is attributable to catalysis already honored in 2005.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed metal-free heterolytic H2 activation and a new family of reactivity, with catalytic hydrogenation and small-molecule activation. It is conceptually simple and chemically new.
assessment.attribution: Stephan's 2006 H2 activation and Erker's intramolecular systems are the central contributions, and the two-person allocation is clean.
assessment.maturity: About 20 years old and well confirmed. Practical synthetic impact is still modest relative to metal catalysis.
uncertainties: Whether the practical use is yet broad enough to justify a prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: ATRP gave a general, controllable route to well-defined polymers of defined architecture, widely used in materials and industry. It is a reaction-design success rather than a single discovery.
assessment.attribution: Matyjaszewski and Sawamoto reported independently in 1995, with Wang as Matyjaszewski's coauthor and Kamigaito in Sawamoto's group. A three-person set must choose between group members, so a precise allocation is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely used, with decades of independent confirmation. Competition with RAFT and NMP as controlled radical methods means impact is shared across several techniques.
uncertainties: Overlap with RAFT (B052) in recognizing controlled radical polymerization.
Fairness of the credit among simultaneous independent discoverers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors apply deaminase chemistry to edit single bases without double-strand breaks and are already in clinical use. At the border with biology, the new chemistry is the protein-engineered conversion and evolution strategy, though it is less clearly molecule-making.
assessment.attribution: Liu directed the work, with Komor (cytosine base editor) and Gaudelli (adenine base editor, requiring evolution of a TadA deaminase) as lead inventors. This is a clear trio, with Nishida and Kondo as a separate Target-AID line.
assessment.maturity: Early (about ten years), though clinical results have already accumulated. Possibly premature versus the larger CRISPR recognition, and whether it counts as chemistry is open.
uncertainties: Premature relative to long-term track record.
Border-field question over what is chemically new.
